rv.q: The performances of the entire company are excellent. Each actor is absolutely convincing, delivering Shakespeare's language naturally and transparently, just as he himself instructed in Hamlet .

But, can Shakespeare’s works translate well for a Sheffield audience today, or does the never ending iambic pentameter make it just a little too confusing? Originally written in 1606, King Lear is a story of power, family, madness and betrayal.

“King Lear” at Crucible Theatre, Sheffield John Murphy in North-East England ★★★★☆ 6 September 2026. There’s a rich tradition of Shakespeare at the Crucible Theatre, one filled with star names and innovative productions, and it’s a history that the current artistic director, Elizabeth Newman, is keen to build on. Ian McDiarmid as King Lear.

Alongside Jay Saighal as Cornwall they are the power couple of the show and the battle for supremacy between the sisters is electrifying. David Birrell as Gloucester was a real highlight, and the way that Yarit Dor worked to show the horror of Gloucester’s most famous scene in the play was brilliant without being gratuitous.
